claim: LLM accuracy on deterministic tasks tracks the probability of the task and of the target output: GPT-4 decodes the common rot-13 cipher far better than rarer shifts (e.g., rot-1 0.82, rot-3 0.76, rot-2 0.02) and decodes rot-13 at 51% when the answer is a high-probability sentence vs 13% when low-probability.

paper.title: Embers of Autoregression: Understanding Large Language Models Through the Problem They are Trained to Solve
paper.venue: PNAS 2024 (per authors; not re-verified in this run)
paper.citation_source: paperclip search (arXiv index) citation field, `paperclip search -s arxiv <title>`; Semantic Scholar API was rate-limited (HTTP 429) throughout this run
paper.s2_batch_record_title: Embers of Autoregression: Understanding Large Language Models Through the Problem They are Trained to Solve

experiment.location_in_paper: Sec 3.1 (Fig 3.1 running example), Sec 4 (tasks, sentences, models), Sec 5.1 (task probability, shift ciphers), Sec 6.1 (output probability), App A.1
experiment.task_or_benchmark: 11 tasks incl. shift-cipher encode/decode, Pig Latin, acronyms, linear functions, sorting, reversal, article swapping, counting, birthdays; sentences of high/medium/low probability (GlobalVoices sentences perturbed with RoBERTa/shuffling).
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: Vary task frequency (rot-13 vs other shifts; common vs rare variants) and output/input probability; zero-shot and prompted variants (prompts in repo stimuli/).
experiment.evaluation_procedure: Temperature 0 via OpenAI API; exact-match accuracy (and edit distance) on 100-sentence sets; spelling control test (99.8-99.9%).
experiment.metric: Accuracy by shift / by output probability bin.
experiment.main_comparison: Common vs rare task variants; high vs low output probability.
experiment.main_result: GPT-4 rot-13 decoding: 0.51 accuracy (high-probability outputs) vs 0.13 (low-probability). Shift-level: rot-13 much easier than smaller shifts; GPT-4 rot-1 0.82, rot-3 0.76, rot-2 0.02. Similar probability effects in Pig Latin, acronyms, linear functions (Celsius-to-Fahrenheit vs rare function), sorting direction, reversal, counting.

downstream.title: When a language model is optimized for reasoning, does it still show embers of autoregression? An analysis of OpenAI o1 (McCoy et al.)
downstream.summary: Read: o1 substantially outperforms previous LLMs but shows the same qualitative trends - shift-cipher accuracy 47% (lowest-probability outputs) vs 92% (highest); common vs rare shift (13 vs 12) differ only for medium/low probability examples; o1 uses far more thinking tokens on rare task variants even when accuracy is equal.

downstream_summary: The authors' own follow-up shows probability sensitivity persists in o1, attenuated in accuracy but visible in token usage. Independent replications on 2025-26 models not located.
notability_notes: Published in PNAS; influential 'teleological' framing; ~widely cited in reasoning-limits work.
gaps: Only author-run follow-up found; independent replication and 2025-26 reasoning models untested. S2 count may be missing.
